text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had learnt that some finance ministry officials were living beyond their means, giving rise to allegations of corruption within the ministry.
-- Selangor state chief minister Abu Hassan Omar said former state executive councillor Aini Taib, who was dropped from the ex-co line-up, must give up all his other public posts.
-- The Health Ministry has confirmed that the virus otbreak which has killed 21 young children in Sarawak state is caused by a virulent strain of the Coxsackie virus B.
-- MBf Capital is poised to emerge a bigger player in financial services with a proposed stake in Suria Capital's Sabah Bank.

-- A new financial crisis at troubled British construction group Costain Group Plc threatens to hit fragile diplomatic and trade relations between Malaysia and Britain, claims British newspaper The Mail on Sunday. Malaysian firm Intria Bhd has a 40 percent stake in Costain.
